It establishes that deferred compensation is allocated to bookkeeping accounts based on the calendar year in which it was earned: one account for all compensation deferred prior to 2015 ("Pre-2015 Class Year Account") and separate accounts for each year from 2015 onward ("Class Year Accounts"). The document also specifies the timing for when deferred compensation is credited to these accounts—generally at the end of each calendar quarter, unless a defined Payment Event occurs, in which case the crediting happens on the Payment Event Date. The terminology for these accounts is clarified for consistent reference throughout the plan.

nodes.title: Section 6. Investment Options
nodes.summary:
This partial document outlines Section 6, "Investment Options," of a plan for Directors, describing how deferred compensation is credited with earnings or losses based on selected hypothetical investment options. The main points covered include:

- Directors can allocate deferred compensation among available investment options, primarily an AFR-Based Option (credited with interest at 120% of the applicable federal rate, compounded daily) and a Share Equivalent Option (credited based on the performance of the Company’s common stock, with deferred amounts converted into Share Equivalent Units or SEUs).
- Directors may choose their allocation at the time of deferral and, unless changed, the election carries forward to subsequent years.
- The AFR-Based Option details how interest is calculated and credited, including valuation at payment events.
- The Share Equivalent Option explains how SEUs are determined, how dividend equivalents are credited, and how SEUs are adjusted for corporate actions (e.g., stock splits, mergers).
- The valuation of SEUs at payment events is specified.
- The Administrator has discretion to allow changes to investment options after a Director’s separation from service, subject to prescribed rules.

For awards from 2015 onward, SEUs are credited to separate "Class Year SEU Award Accounts" for each calendar year. SEUs awarded for years prior to 2015 are credited to a "Pre-2015 Class Year Account," either existing or newly created, and are managed under the Share Equivalent Option. The document also specifies that SEUs for each year are credited at times set by the SEU Plan and are subsequently adjusted, valued, and paid in the same manner as other SEUs. Additionally, after a Director’s separation from service, the Administrator may permit changes to investment options for these accounts, subject to prescribed rules and restrictions.

The document also references compliance with Section 409A and specifies that elections apply to both the Class Year Account and Class Year SEU Award Account.

All payments under this section are to be made in a lump sum. The section also references the authority of the Administrator to set terms and procedures for beneficiary designations.

nodes.title: Section 10. Time and Amount of Payment

nodes.title: Section 11. Director's Rights Unsecured

## Section 11. Director's Rights Unsecured

The right of any Director to receive future payments under the provisions of this Plan shall be an unsecured, contractual claim against the general assets of the Company. This Plan shall be unfunded. The Company shall not be required to establish any special or separate fund or to make any segregation of assets for the payment of any amounts under this Plan.

Participants may not sell, transfer, assign, pledge, levy, attach, encumber or alienate any amounts payable under this Plan.

nodes.title: Section 12. Statement of Account

The Company will provide or make available to each Director a statement of account that will confirm the Director's Class Year Account and Class Year SEU Award Account balance(s) as of the end of the preceding quarter, or on such more frequent basis as determined by the Administrator. The Administrator may provide for such statement of accounts to be in writing (including electronic format) or by means of access to such information in electronic format.

nodes.title: Section 13. Amendment

## Section 13. Amendment

This Plan may be amended at any time and from time to time by the Board of Directors of the Company; provided, however, that the Board of Directors may not adopt any amendment that would (a) materially and adversely affect any right of or benefit to any Director with respect to any of the benefits theretofore credited without such Director's written consent, or (b) result in a violation of Section 409A. Any amendment to this Plan that would cause a violation of Section 409A shall be null and void and of no effect.

nodes.title: Section 14. Termination

Upon termination, the distribution of existing Class Year Accounts and Class Year SEU Award Accounts will proceed according to the Plan's provisions and each Director's payment election as they existed before termination. However, the Board may choose to accelerate payments of these accounts upon termination, provided such acceleration complies with specific treasury regulations (Section 1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)).

nodes.summary: This partial document is from Article 2, "Definitions," of a plan document, likely related to employee benefits or a deferred compensation plan for American Express (Amex). It provides detailed definitions of key terms used throughout the plan, including but not limited to: types of accounts (Deferral Account, Supplemental Account), roles and committees (Administrator, Committee, Investment Committee), participant classifications (Executive Officer, Non-Executive Officer, Retiree, Participant), types of benefits (Deferral Benefits, Supplemental Benefits, Grandfathered and Degrandfathered Benefits), relevant compensation terms (Base Salary, Incentive Pay), plan years, eligibility criteria (Retirement Eligible, Disability), references to related plans (Qualified Retirement Plan, Severance Plan), and legal references (Section 409A, Code, Exchange Act). The section also clarifies the use of gender and number in the document and states that undefined capitalized terms will have the meanings assigned in related Qualified Retirement Plans. The definitions establish the framework for interpreting the rights, obligations, and procedures described in the rest of the plan.

nodes.title:
ARTICLE 3
ADMINISTRATION
nodes.summary: This partial document outlines the administration of a Plan under Article 3. It specifies that the Plan is to be administered by an Administrator, who is granted full authority, power, and discretion to interpret, construe, and manage the Plan. The Administrator's decisions are binding on all participants and beneficiaries. The Administrator is empowered to correct errors, supply omissions, and reconcile inconsistencies in the Plan as deemed necessary. Additionally, the Administrator may delegate their authority and responsibilities to others, with such delegates having the same powers to the extent of the delegation.

nodes.title:
ARTICLE 4
ELIGIBILITY
nodes.summary: This partial document outlines the eligibility criteria for participation in a specific employee benefit plan. It specifies that only certain employees, generally those in higher pay bands (Band 35 or above), are eligible, subject to the Administrator's discretion to exclude certain employees or groups. To participate, employees must also be participants in a Qualified Retirement Plan maintained by the company and meet additional requirements for the relevant plan year, such as having an existing account, earning above a specified compensation limit, holding a high-level position (Band 50 or above), or accruing retirement benefits above certain IRS limits. The document emphasizes compliance with ERISA "top-hat" plan requirements and allows for some administrative flexibility in determining eligibility.

nodes.title:
ARTICLE 5
SUPPLEMENTAL BENEFITS
nodes.summary:
This partial document outlines the provisions for supplemental retirement benefits under Article 5, focusing on benefits that exceed the standard limits of the company's primary retirement plans (the RP and RSP). The main points covered include:

1. **Supplemental Benefits for RP Participants (Section 5.1):**
   - Establishment of an RP-Related Account for eligible participants.
   - Definition and possible expansion of "Compensation" for crediting purposes, including restricted stock awards.
   - Calculation of contribution credits to make up for limits imposed by qualified plan rules, with credits ceasing after July 1, 2007.
   - Uniform application of benefit formulas.
   - Provision for certain participants to receive credit for additional years of service, subject to vesting and forfeiture rules, and special agreements.

2. **Supplemental Benefits for RSP Participants (Section 5.2):**
   - Establishment of an RSP-Related Account for eligible participants.
   - Definition of "Compensation" for RSP credits, with specific limitations for higher-level employees and rules for disregarding temporary salary reductions.
   - Detailed rules for various types of supplemental contributions, including:
     - Company stock contributions (with credits ceasing after July 1, 2007).
     - Company profit-sharing contributions, subject to vesting and forfeiture.
     - Company matching contributions, including special rules for amounts limited by IRS regulations and vesting aligned with the RSP.
     - Company conversion contributions, with eligibility and timing restrictions.
     - Transition contributions for certain former employees, with coordination to avoid duplication and expiration of eligibility.
     - Explicit exclusion of disability-related contributions.
   - Provision for additional years of service credit for certain participants, subject to vesting, forfeiture, and special agreements.

Overall, the document details how supplemental accounts are credited to eligible participants to provide retirement benefits in excess of qualified plan limits, the definitions and limitations of compensation used for these credits, the types of supplemental contributions available, and the vesting and forfeiture conditions that apply.

nodes.title: Section 5.3 Crediting of Account.
nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines procedures and rules regarding the crediting of accounts and the payment of supplemental benefits under a retirement or deferred compensation plan. Key points include:

- **Crediting of Accounts (Section 5.3):**  
  - The timing and manner of crediting amounts to participants’ supplemental accounts are determined by the plan administrator, generally aiming to mirror the timing of similar qualified plans but with flexibility.
  - Special rules apply for credits related to Section 415 limitations and special agreements, including estimation and timing of credits.
  - Company stock contributions and other types of contributions (profit-sharing, matching, conversion, transition, and special agreement credits) are credited to specific subaccounts, with restrictions on stock fund allocations and self-directed brokerage accounts.
  - The administrator has discretion to establish additional reserve accounts and determine procedures for reflecting gains, losses, and other account changes.

- **Supplemental Benefits Payment Election (Section 5.4):**  
  - Participants may elect the form of payment (lump sum or installments) for their supplemental benefits, subject to rules and deadlines set by the administrator and compliance with Section 409A.
  - Detailed rules govern initial and modified elections, including special provisions for participants under prior plans, new participants, and rehired employees.
  - If a participant fails to make a timely election, a default lump-sum payment election applies.
  - Only one modification to the initial payment election is allowed, subject to specific timing and deferral requirements, and no changes are permitted after separation from service (with exceptions for rehired employees).
  - Automatic elections and default rules are specified for new participants and certain company contributions, with clear limitations on further modifications.

Overall, the document details the administrative processes for crediting supplemental retirement accounts and the options and limitations for participants to elect how their supplemental benefits are paid.

nodes.title:
ARTICLE 6
ELECTIVE DEFERRALS
nodes.summary: This partial document outlines the rules and procedures for employee participation in elective deferral benefits under a specific plan, focusing on eligibility notification, participation criteria, and special enrollment provisions. It details how employees are notified of eligibility, the conditions under which they may participate (including employment band requirements and timing), and the process for making deferral elections. The document also addresses special rules for employees who become newly eligible during the plan year, including those who exceed certain compensation limits or who have previously participated in similar deferred compensation arrangements. Restrictions on mid-year elections and the irrevocability of deferral elections are also specified, along with references to compliance with Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code.

nodes.title: Section 6.4 Deferrable Compensation.
nodes.summary: This partial document outlines the rules and procedures for deferrable compensation under Section 6.4. It specifies the types of compensation eligible for deferral, including base salary and incentive pay, and details the timing and conditions under which employees can elect to defer these amounts. The document distinguishes between regular eligible employees and those who become eligible mid-year, providing different calculation methods for each. It sets maximum limits on the amounts that can be deferred, both as a percentage and in dollar terms, and allows the plan administrator discretion to impose further limits or waive certain restrictions. The document also describes how deferral amounts may be computed, either as percentages or dollar amounts, and addresses the application of deferral elections in relation to IRS compensation limits.

nodes.title: Section 6.5 Deferral Benefits Election.
nodes.summary:
This partial document outlines the procedures and requirements for employees to elect deferral benefits under a specific plan. Key points include:

- The timing and deadlines for making an irrevocable deferral election, generally by December 15 of the preceding year, with provisions for mid-year elections for newly eligible employees.
- The required form and content of the deferral election, including specification of compensation items and amounts to be deferred, subject to plan limits.
- Special rules for employees in "Band 50 or above," allowing them to elect the timing (either upon separation from service or a specified future date) and form (lump sum or installments) of payment for their deferral benefits.
- Default provisions if an employee fails to specify valid payment timing or form.
- Restrictions on lower-band employees, who cannot make special elections regarding payment timing or form, with their deferral benefits subject to standard plan provisions.
- Procedures for withholding deferred amounts from salary and incentive pay.
- The establishment and maintenance of individual deferral accounts for participants, with possible subaccounts for tracking earnings and losses.

nodes.title:
ARTICLE 7
EARNINGS
nodes.summary:
## ARTICLE 7
EARNINGS Section 7.1 RP-Related Account. For each Participant, the RP-Related Account established pursuant to Section 5.1 shall be increased by the Imputed Earnings Credit (as such term is defined in the RP), not less frequently than annually, under procedures and at times determined by the Administrator and consistently applied for similarly situated Participants. Such earnings shall be credited at the same interest rate and computed in a similar manner (to the extent administratively feasible) as Imputed Earnings Credits are computed under the RP for each Plan Year. Section 7.2 RSP-Related Account. A Participant's RSP-Related Account shall be credited with earnings under the Hypothetical Investment Method set forth below.

nodes.title: Section 7.3 Deferral Accounts.
nodes.summary: This partial document outlines the methods for crediting earnings to Participants' Deferral Benefits under a plan, distinguishing between Plan Years before and after 2011. It specifies that, starting in 2011, Deferral Benefits are credited using a Hypothetical Investment Method, while prior years use an Interest Method, with special rules and limitations based on participant status (Executive Officer, Non-Executive Officer, or Retiree). The document also addresses transitions between methods, exceptions based on payment timing, and limitations tied to Amex's Return on Equity (ROE) and the Applicable Federal Rate (AFR).

nodes.title: Section 7.4 Hypothetical Investment Method.
nodes.summary:
This partial document outlines the rules and procedures for the Hypothetical Investment Method and the Interest Method as they apply to participants' RSP-Related and Deferral Accounts in a retirement or deferred compensation plan. Key points include:

- Participants can direct how their accounts are allocated among various subaccounts, subject to certain restrictions, such as a maximum of ten percent of account value or new contributions being invested in the Stock Fund.
- Elections and changes to investment allocations must be made in specified increments and may be amended according to plan rules.
- The performance of each subaccount reflects the performance of the corresponding investment fund, including gains, losses, and dividends, or, in the case of the AFR option, the applicable federal rate.
- If a participant does not make an investment election, a default fund designated by the Administrator will be used.
- The Administrator has discretion to limit available investment options and to establish valuation procedures for subaccounts.
- Under the Interest Method, Deferral Accounts are credited with interest equivalents at a scheduled rate, with specific vesting rules for principal and earnings, including full vesting of all earnings after December 31, 2010.

nodes.title: Section 7.6 Special Restrictions.
nodes.summary: This partial document outlines special restrictions applicable to "Insiders" under Section 7.6 of a plan, particularly regarding their accounts and transactions involving a Stock Fund. The main points covered include: (1) defining the periods during which these restrictions apply to Insiders, including after they cease to be Insiders if reporting obligations continue under Rule 16a-2(b) of the Exchange Act; (2) prohibiting Insiders from making or transferring credits to subaccounts reflecting the Stock Fund's performance, with limited exceptions for distributions due to payment elections, death, or forfeiture provisions, and only when permitted by securities rules; and (3) stating the intent that such account credits qualify for exemption from Section 16 under Rule 16b-3(d) of the Exchange Act, with the plan administrator required to interpret and administer the plan accordingly for Insiders.

nodes.title:
ARTICLE 8
PAYMENT OF BENEFITS
nodes.summary:
## ARTICLE 8
PAYMENT OF BENEFITS

nodes.title: Section 8.1 Supplemental Account Payments (Other than Payments Due to Death or Disability).
nodes.summary: This partial document outlines the rules for payment of Supplemental Account Benefits to participants who separate from service for reasons other than death or disability. It specifies that payment timing and form (lump sum or annual installments) depend on the participant’s election, with lump sums paid at least six months after separation and installments beginning the following July 1, both subject to administrative timing limits. It addresses the impact of modifications to the participant’s initial election, including a mandatory five-year payment delay for amended elections (except for benefits under the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election, which cannot be modified or delayed). The document also details how annual installment amounts are calculated and clarifies that only vested portions of the account are payable, with non-vested amounts forfeited. Re-employment after separation does not alter the payment schedule.

nodes.title: Section 8.2 Deferral Account Payments (Other than Payments Due to Death or Disability).
nodes.summary:
This partial document outlines the rules and procedures for the payment of deferral account benefits under a deferred compensation plan, specifically addressing payments not due to death or disability. The main points covered include:

- The distinction between Pre-2011 and Post-2010 Deferral Benefits, with different payment timing and procedures for each.
- Rules for participants (specifically employees in Band 50 or above) who have elected to receive their deferral benefits on a specified date, including options for lump-sum or annual installment payments, and the timing of such payments.
- Procedures for payment upon a participant’s Separation from Service, differentiating between those who are Retirement Eligible and those who are not, and specifying how remaining installments or lump sums are paid depending on the participant’s status and prior elections.
- The calculation method for annual installment payments, using a fractional approach based on the number of remaining payments.
- A limitation that only vested portions of a participant’s deferral account will be paid, with nonvested amounts forfeited.
- Rules for the designation, revocation, and modification of beneficiaries for deferral and supplemental accounts, including automatic revocation of spousal beneficiary designations upon divorce, and the process for re-designating a former spouse as beneficiary if desired.
- Clarification that the plan is not liable for payments made to a beneficiary prior to notification of divorce.

nodes.title: Section 8.4 Death.
nodes.summary: This partial document outlines the procedures for the distribution of a Participant's Supplemental Account and Deferral Account upon the Participant's death. It specifies that payments are to be made to the designated Beneficiary or Beneficiaries, with timing dependent on whether the Participant was actively employed or had separated from service at the time of death. The document details the payment schedules, including lump-sum payments on specific dates (either January 1/July 1 or March 15/September 15, depending on the type and timing of deferral benefits), and clarifies the handling of annual installment elections if the Participant dies before or after installments have commenced. It also addresses situations where payment elections had been modified, ensuring that death benefits are paid promptly and not subject to previously elected deferral extensions. The provisions distinguish between Pre-2011 and Post-2010 Deferral Benefits, each with its own payment timing rules.

nodes.title: Section 8.5 Disability.
nodes.summary:
The partial document outlines the rules and procedures for distributions from a participant’s account under a benefits plan in the event of disability, unforeseeable emergency, company offsets, tax withholding, and de minimis lump sum payments. Specifically, it details:

- How disability triggers payment of supplemental and deferral accounts, with timing and form of payment (lump sum or installments) depending on participant elections and whether benefits are pre-2011 or post-2010.
- The process for participants to request payouts due to unforeseeable emergencies, including limits on payout amounts and conditions under which such payouts are allowed.
- The company’s right to offset amounts due to the participant to recover debts or enforce company policies, subject to legal restrictions.
- The company’s obligation to withhold applicable taxes from any payments made under the plan.
- The administrator’s discretion to make a mandatory lump sum payout of small account balances, subject to regulatory limits and plan termination requirements.

nodes.title:
ARTICLE 9
CHANGE IN CONTROL
nodes.summary:
This partial document covers Article 9, which addresses the concept of "Change in Control" for Amex. It defines what constitutes a Change in Control, including specific thresholds for ownership changes, board composition changes, major corporate transactions (such as mergers, reorganizations, or asset sales), and shareholder approval of liquidation or dissolution. The document details exceptions and clarifications for each scenario.

Section 9.2 outlines the effects of a Change in Control on participant accounts under the plan. It mandates the transfer of account values to a trust, changes the investment method for certain accounts, and specifies how earnings are credited post-Change in Control. It also addresses vesting for participants who separate from service after a Change in Control.

Additionally, the document discusses the handling of "golden parachute" excise taxes under Section 4999 of the Internal Revenue Code, including potential reductions in payments to avoid excise tax liability, the process for determining whether payments are subject to the tax, and the role of an independent accounting firm in these determinations. The company is required to provide participants with detailed calculations and explanations if their payments are to be reduced.

nodes.title:
ARTICLE 10
CLAIMS PROCEDURES
nodes.summary:
## ARTICLE 10
CLAIMS PROCEDURES

nodes.title: Section 10.1 Claim.
nodes.summary: This partial document outlines the procedures for making a claim under a benefits plan. It specifies that a claimant who believes they are being denied benefits or has another claim related to the plan must submit a written request or description of the claim to the plan administrator. The document also sets time limits for initiating legal action: no action can be started later than 90 days after a final appeal denial or one year from when the cause of action accrued, whichever comes first. It defines when a cause of action accrues and designates the administrator as the agent for service of process. Additionally, it requires claimants to exhaust all internal remedies under the plan’s claims procedures before seeking further relief.

nodes.title: Section 10.2 Claim Decision.
nodes.summary: This partial document outlines the procedures and requirements for the decision-making process regarding claims under a benefit plan. It specifies the timeframes within which the Administrator must respond to claims (generally 90 days, with possible extensions), the information that must be included in a denial notice (such as reasons for denial, relevant plan provisions, additional required information, steps for review, and legal rights), and special procedures and timelines for claims involving determinations of disability. For disability-related claims, it details shorter response periods, possible extensions, requirements for advance notice, and additional information that must be provided in denial notices, including discussions of medical and vocational evidence, internal guidelines, and explanations for exclusions or limitations based on medical necessity.

nodes.title: Section 10.3 Request for Review.
nodes.summary: This partial document outlines the procedures for a claimant to request a review of an Administrator’s determination regarding a claim. It specifies that, generally, a claimant has 60 days after receiving a written explanation to request a review in writing, with access to relevant documents provided free of charge, subject to certain legal privileges. If the claim involves a determination of the participant’s disabled status, the claimant has 180 days to request a review. Failure to request a review within the applicable time frame bars the claimant from challenging the determination.

nodes.title: Section 10.4 Review of Decision.
nodes.summary: This partial document outlines the procedures and requirements for the review of benefit claim decisions under a Plan, including the claimant's rights and the Administrator's obligations. It details the process for issuing written decisions on claims, including timeframes, required content of denial notices, and the claimant's right to access relevant documents. Special procedures are described for claims involving determinations of disability, such as ensuring impartial review, consulting appropriate medical professionals, and providing detailed explanations for denials. The document also addresses the right to compel binding arbitration for most claims (with exceptions for disability determinations and where prohibited by law), specifying that arbitration must follow Plan and Policy terms, including prohibitions on class actions. The burden of proof for claims based on facts not in Plan records is placed on the claimant, who must provide satisfactory evidence. Finally, the Administrator is granted sole and exclusive authority over all matters in this section, with no interference from the Committee.

nodes.title:
ARTICLE 11
AMENDMENT \& TERMINATION
nodes.summary: This partial document covers Article 11, which addresses the amendment and termination of a Plan. It outlines the authority of the Committee to amend or terminate the Plan, with restrictions to protect the benefits of current participants and beneficiaries. Amendments cannot violate Section 409A regulations, particularly regarding definitions that could affect deferral elections. Upon termination of the Plan, no further contributions are allowed, and account distributions must follow the procedures specified in Article 8 and comply with Section 409A. The Committee has discretion over the timing and manner of distributions after termination, but must act within legal constraints.

nodes.title:
ARTICLE 12
GENERAL PROVISIONS
nodes.summary: This partial document covers the general provisions of a deferred compensation plan. It clarifies that the plan is unfunded, meaning participants have no greater claim than general unsecured creditors and no trust or fiduciary relationship is created. The document states that participants' rights to deferred compensation are non-transferable except by law. It specifies that participation does not guarantee continued employment. Deferred compensation under the plan is not considered salary or compensation for other employee benefit plans unless explicitly stated. Finally, the plan is intended to comply with Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code, and will be administered and interpreted to maintain such compliance.

nodes.title: Section 12.6 No Guarantee of Tax Consequences.
nodes.summary: This partial document outlines several key provisions related to a deferred compensation plan. It states that the company does not guarantee or make any representations regarding the tax consequences for participants or their beneficiaries, and that any payments made under the plan are binding and discharge the company from further claims. The document also clarifies that no person associated with the plan guarantees any specific tax treatment for deferred amounts or distributions. Additionally, it limits the company’s liability, specifying that participation in the plan does not grant legal or equitable rights beyond those provided by law or the plan itself, and that the company does not guarantee against losses or specific investment outcomes. The document further includes a severability clause ensuring that if any provision is found invalid, the remainder of the plan remains effective, and notes that section headings are for convenience only. Finally, it establishes that the plan is governed by the laws of the State of New York, except where superseded by federal law.

nodes.title: SCHEDULE A
nodes.summary: ## SCHEDULE A

nodes.title: DEFERRAL ACCOUNT SCHEDULE RATE
nodes.summary: This partial document outlines the method for determining the interest rate (Schedule Rate) credited to participants' Deferral Accounts under a plan, based on American Express's (Amex's) annual Return on Equity (ROE) relative to its announced ROE Target Range. The Schedule Rate varies: if Amex's ROE is below the target range, the rate is Moody's A Rate; within the range, 9%; and above the range, 11%. The credited amounts are subject to caps, particularly for Executive Officers, as specified in Article 7 of the Plan. Definitions for "ROE" and "ROE Target Range" are provided, and the Committee retains discretion to adjust the Schedule Rate prospectively or retrospectively without prior notice. Schedule B is reserved and contains no content.

nodes.title: SCHEDULE C
nodes.summary: ## SCHEDULE C

nodes.title: Prior Deferral Plan Benefit Payment Appendix
nodes.summary: This partial document outlines Schedule C, an appendix detailing the payment timing rules for Deferral Plan benefits related to years before 2011, which are governed by earlier deferral plans now consolidated into the current Plan. It clarifies that the timing and form of benefit payments remain as specified in the original governing plan documents, and in case of any conflict, those documents take precedence. The appendix is intended for administrative use and may be updated by the Administrator, but cannot change the timing or form of payments or violate Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code. Payment dates are approximate, allowing for payments within 90 days of the specified date, in line with Treasury Regulations.

nodes.title: Pre-2008 Deferral Plans
nodes.summary: This partial document discusses the treatment of pre-2008 deferral plans, specifically focusing on amounts earned and vested as of December 31, 2004, which are considered "grandfathered" and exempt from Section 409A. It details which principal and interest amounts qualify as grandfathered based on the year earned and the participant's retirement eligibility status as of the end of 2004. The document clarifies that the grandfathered status mainly affects employees receiving severance payments and distinguishes between the definitions of "termination of employment" for grandfathered and non-grandfathered benefits. It also notes that the rules for these pre-2008 benefits are not included in Article 8 of the Plan, which only covers benefits from 2008 onward.

nodes.title: If a Participant elected to be paid at a specified date or as of retirement $+\mathbf{X}$ years ( $\mathbf{X}$ could be up to 10)
nodes.summary: This partial document outlines the payment rules for participants in a plan who have elected to receive their benefits at a specified date or a certain number of years after retirement (up to 10 years). It details the timing and form of payments (lump sum or installments) based on various scenarios, including whether the participant is still employed, becomes retirement eligible, or terminates employment before the elected payment date. The document specifies payment schedules (March 15/September 15), addresses what happens if termination occurs during the payment period, and notes special considerations for severance situations and grandfathered amounts. Examples are provided to clarify how the rules apply in different circumstances.

nodes.title: - If the Participant elected to be paid at retirement
nodes.summary: This partial document outlines the payment options for participants upon retirement or termination. It specifies that if a participant is "Retirement Eligible" (defined as at least age 55 with at least 10 years of service), they can choose to receive their benefit as either a lump sum or in installments, with payments beginning on the first March 15 or September 15 at least six months after retirement. If installments are chosen, subsequent payments occur each March 15. If the participant is not retirement eligible at termination, payment is made as a lump sum on the first March 15 or September 15 at least six months after termination. The document also notes that severance may affect the timing of payments, particularly for grandfathered amounts, and refers to a Severance Flow Chart for further guidance.

nodes.title: - If the Participant leaves the Company as a result of Disability
nodes.summary:
## - If the Participant leaves the Company as a result of Disability

- The Participant will be paid according to elections.
- If lump sum elected, paid in a lump sum on the first March 15/September 15 that is at least 6 months following date of disability.
- If installments elected, payments begin on the first March 15/September 15 that is at least 6 months following date of disability; subsequent installments will be paid on each March 15 .

nodes.title: - If the Participant dies before payments begin or before receiving all installments
nodes.summary:
## - If the Participant dies before payments begin or before receiving all installments

- The balance of the Participant's account will be paid as a lump sum to the Participant's designated beneficiary on the first March 15/September 15 that is at least 6 months following date of death.

nodes.title: 2008-2010 Plans
nodes.summary:
## 2008-2010 Plans

These plans do not include any "grandfathered" money and are subject to Section 409A of the Code in their entirety. The rules governing these benefits are set forth in Article 8 of the Plan document as the rules applicable to "Pre-2011 Deferral Benefits."

nodes.title: - If the Participant elected to be paid on a specified date
nodes.summary: This partial document outlines the payment procedures for participants who have elected to receive benefits on a specified date under a deferred compensation or retirement plan. It details how payments are made depending on whether the participant separates from service before or after the specified date, and whether they are retirement eligible at the time of separation. The document specifies the timing and form of payments (lump sum or installments), the impact of separation from service on payment schedules, and clarifies that severance status does not affect benefit payments. It also notes a change from pre-2008 rules regarding payment delays.

nodes.title: - If the Participant elected to be paid at retirement
nodes.summary: This partial document outlines the payment options and timing for participants who have elected to receive benefits at retirement. It specifies different procedures based on whether the participant is retirement eligible at the time of separation from service, including lump sum and installment payment options, both commencing at least six months after separation. It clarifies that severance status does not impact benefit payments for these years, as none are grandfathered, and details that standard death or disability benefit rules apply for pre-2011 deferral benefits.

nodes.title: Special Rule for Degrandfathered Participants' Degrandfathered Benefits Under Section 1.3 of the Plan
nodes.summary:
## Special Rule for Degrandfathered Participants' Degrandfathered Benefits Under Section 1.3 of the Plan

These rules apply to degradfathered principal only. Interest for the relevant years was never grandfathered, and hence is not affected by the degradfathering transition. For the interest portion of the account balance, see the rules for Pre-2008 Deferral Plan benefits.

nodes.title: - If the Participant did NOT Make an election regarding degradfathered benefits
nodes.summary: This partial document outlines the payment procedures for participants who did not make an election regarding grandfathered benefits. It details the timing and form of benefit payments, including lump sum and installment options, based on whether a specified date was elected and the participant's separation from service. The document specifies earliest possible payment dates, how payments are handled if separation occurs before or after the specified date, and clarifies that separation from service does not alter the payment schedule once begun. It also addresses the handling of benefits in the event of the participant's death, referencing standard death benefit rules for Post-2010 Deferral Benefits.

nodes.title: SCHEDULE D
nodes.summary: This partial document outlines the irrevocable termination of a specific Plan, contingent upon the closing of a transaction between American Express Travel Related Services Company, Inc. and a subsidiary of Time Inc. The termination applies only to employees of American Express Publishing Corporation who are participants in the Plan as of the termination date. It specifies that all account crediting for these participants will cease on the termination date, and accrued benefits will be paid out within twelve months in accordance with Treasury regulations and the Plan's provisions, ensuring compliance with Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code.

nodes.title: SCHEDULE E
nodes.summary: ## SCHEDULE E

nodes.title: American Express Global Business Travel Divestiture
nodes.summary: This partial document outlines provisions related to the divestiture of American Express Global Business Travel and the establishment of a joint venture. It specifies how plan participation and benefits will be managed for employees who become part of the new business entity, ensuring they receive benefits comparable to those previously offered by American Express for a certain period. The document clarifies that, in case of conflicts, these provisions take precedence for affected employees, but do not alter benefits accrued before the schedule's applicability.

nodes.title:
ARTICLE 1
CONTINUED PARTICIPATION
nodes.summary: The partial document outlines the rules for continued participation in a benefits plan for Business Employees following a transition from the Company to a separate Business entity. It covers eligibility requirements for continued participation, including prior participation or timely enrollment, and notes that participation is limited to select management or highly compensated employees to maintain "top-hat" plan status under ERISA. The document also details circumstances under which participation and contributions will terminate, such as separation from service or the end of the period for comparable benefits, and addresses the impact of a Business Employee returning to Company employment on their plan participation. The Administrator has discretion to exclude individuals, provided compliance with Section 409A is maintained.

nodes.title:
ARTICLE 2
CONTRIBUTIONS
nodes.summary: This partial document outlines the rules and provisions regarding contributions under a benefits plan for Business Employees. It covers the following main points: (1) the process for deducting Deferral Benefits from Base Salary and Incentive Pay based on employee elections, including definitions and aggregation rules for compensation; (2) the allocation of Supplemental Benefits to employee accounts at the discretion of Amex, with consideration of amounts paid by the Business; (3) a prohibition on duplicative benefits for employees; and (4) clarification that all benefits under the plan are unfunded obligations of the Company, with any funding arrangements not granting participants preferential rights over general creditors, thereby maintaining the plan’s unfunded status.

nodes.title:
ARTICLE 3
VESTING
nodes.summary:
## ARTICLE 3
VESTING Vesting of benefits shall be determined in the same fashion as if employment with the Business were employment with the Company, and the vesting of contributions shall be accelerated to the extent the vesting of similar contributions is accelerated under the RSP with respect to Business Employees; provided, however, that with respect to Company contributions attributable to employment with the Business, the normal vesting schedule applicable to comparable contributions under the Business' 401(k) plan shall apply and vesting will not be accelerated.

nodes.title:
ARTICLE 4
EARNINGS
nodes.summary:
## ARTICLE 4
EARNINGS Credits to a Participant's Deferral Account and RSP-Related Account with respect to benefits earned while a Business Employee shall be made in accordance with Article 7 of the Plan.

nodes.title:
ARTICLE 5
PAYMENT OF BENEFITS
nodes.summary: This partial document outlines the rules for payment of benefits to employees who transition between employment with a "Business" and the "Company" under a benefit plan. It specifies that such transitions do not, by themselves, trigger a separation from service or a new participation period, unless required by Section 409A of the tax code. The document also details how separations from service are determined for Business Employees, including the treatment of affiliates and the need to adjust definitions in the event of future transactions. Additionally, it clarifies that a participant's beneficiary designation remains unchanged if they become a Business Employee.

nodes.title:
ARTICLE 6
